cards.text: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, is writing a letter to the saints at Philippi (Philippians 1:1). Now he writes "Finally," and friend, this letter still has a LOT of road left. That's me yelling "LAST batch!" and then baking four more.

cards.question: Paul calls them his brothers. What does he tell them to do in the Lord?

cards.text: Then Paul admits he's about to write them the same things again. Listen, I respect a man who repeats himself, because I've given this oven the same pep talk every morning for YEARS.

cards.question: Paul says writing the same things to the Philippians again is a lot of trouble for him.
Paul says writing the same things again is no trouble for him. What does he say it is for the Philippians?

cards.text: Then Paul's tone flips HARD: "Watch out for those dogs, those workers of evil, those mutilators of the flesh!" Rejoice one second, RED ALERT the next, like me spotting a baker's sleeve drifting toward a hot oven.
Then Paul says, "it is we who are the circumcision," and he describes that group. First off, they worship by the Spirit of God.

cards.question: Paul says the circumcision worship by the Spirit of God. Who does he say they glory in?
Paul says the circumcision put great confidence in the flesh.

cards.text: Then Paul says he could have that kind of confidence in the flesh himself. Hold on to your apron, friend.

cards.question: Paul says he could have confidence in the flesh himself. If anyone else thinks he has grounds for that confidence, how much does Paul say he has?

cards.text: And out comes Paul's résumé: circumcised on the eighth day, of the people of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews, and as to the law, a Pharisee. Meanwhile MY résumé says "found at the bottom of a bin, 25 cents."
As to zeal, Paul says he was persecuting the church. Friend, that's a line I'd leave OFF my résumé, but Paul puts it right there on the list.

cards.question: As to righteousness in the law, Paul says he was faultless.

cards.text: Paul lets that whole list sit there for a second... and then he writes one little word: "But."

cards.question: Paul says whatever was gain to him, he now counts as loss for the sake of Christ.

cards.text: And Paul goes BIGGER, friend. Not just the résumé, but ALL things he counts as loss, and he says he has lost all things for Christ.

cards.question: Paul counts all things as loss compared to the surpassing excellence of what?
How does Paul say he considers all the things he lost?

cards.text: RUBBISH. Paul takes the most stacked résumé in the room and treats it like an old takeout menu from my junk drawer, all so he may gain Christ and be found in Him.

cards.question: Paul doesn't want his own righteousness from the ___. He wants the righteousness from God that comes through ___ in Christ.

cards.text: Then Paul says what he wants now, and it's NOT his old title back. He wants to know Christ and the power of His resurrection.

cards.question: Paul says he also wants the fellowship of Christ's sufferings, being conformed to Him in His death.
Paul wants to know Christ in His resurrection and His sufferings. Where does Paul hope all of this leads?

cards.text: Notice the little word Paul tucks in there: somehow. I'll be honest, friend, that little word is gonna stick with me tonight while the ovens cool.

findings.problem: The card says Paul "admits" he's about to write the same things again. Philippians 3:1 doesn't frame it as an admission. Paul simply says "It is no trouble for me to write the same things to you again." Calling it an admission suggests reluctance, which also steers the baker toward the wrong answer (True) on card 4.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The question refers to "the circumcision" as if it were a third-party group. Paul's words are "it is we who are the circumcision" (Philippians 3:3). Paul is naming believers, himself included. Dropping the "we" makes the term read like circumcised people in general.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The statement says "the circumcision put great confidence in the flesh" without Paul's "we" (Philippians 3:3). Card 6 has just warned about "mutilators of the flesh," so a baker can reasonably read "the circumcision" as that group and mark True. The card should make clear this is Paul's own "we."

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: "Paul lets that whole list sit there for a second" adds a pause in time that Philippians 3:7 doesn't give.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The question says Paul wants "to know Christ in His resurrection and His sufferings." Philippians 3:10 says he wants "to know Christ and the power of His resurrection and the fellowship of His sufferings." The paraphrase drops "the power of" and "the fellowship of," and that changes what Paul says he wants to know.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
